root_cause.text: `bpf_prog_test_run_skb()` in the BPF test-run path used `skb->protocol` to unconditionally derive IPv4/IPv6 socket fields and could dereference `ip_hdr(skb)`/`ipv6_hdr(skb)` even when `skb_headlen(skb)` contained only an Ethernet header, because it lacked a length check before accessing network-layer headers.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the IPv4/IPv6 header-size validation into the `switch (skb->protocol)` and returns `-EINVAL` when `skb_headlen(skb) < sizeof(struct iphdr)` or `< sizeof(struct ipv6hdr)` before calling `ip_hdr(skb)`/`ipv6_hdr(skb)`; the CVE text explicitly says the function "may access ip_hdr(skb) or ipv6_hdr(skb) even when the provided test input only contains an Ethernet header."

intent_record.intent_summary: Reject truncated IPv4/IPv6 skbs in bpf_prog_test_run_skb before reading header fields.
intent_record.what: In the IPv4 and IPv6 protocol cases, the code now checks whether `skb_headlen(skb)` is smaller than the size of the corresponding IP header before accessing header fields. If the linear head is too short, it sets `ret = -EINVAL` and jumps to `out`. The assignments to `sk->sk_family`, source address, and destination address were moved to occur only after this length check. The IPv4 and IPv6 header field reads are no longer conditionally skipped; they are now always executed after the validation succeeds.
intent_record.how: This prevents the function from reading IPv4 or IPv6 header fields when the skb does not contain a full header in its linear data area, avoiding invalid memory access and ensuring the test run fails with `-EINVAL` for truncated packets. For valid packets, behavior remains the same, with socket family and address fields populated from the packet headers.

grouping_result.intent: Reject truncated IPv4/IPv6 skbs in bpf_prog_test_run_skb before reading header fields.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it adds a length check in bpf_prog_test_run_skb to reject truncated IPv4/IPv6 skbs before accessing network-layer headers, preventing the unsafe dereference.

candidates.rationale: This IPv4 branch unconditionally derives socket state from skb->protocol before any robust truncation rejection; in the vulnerable path it led into accesses of ip_hdr(skb) when only an Ethernet header was present.
This IPv6 branch similarly derives socket state based solely on skb->protocol and could proceed toward ipv6_hdr(skb) access even when the packet was too short.
This is the direct dereference of the IPv4 network header that becomes unsafe when skb_headlen(skb) contains only an Ethernet header.
This is another direct IPv4 header dereference that can read past the available linear data in truncated skbs.
This is the direct IPv6 header dereference implicated by the lack of a length check before accessing network-layer fields.

vuln_statements.explanation: This directly dereferences the IPv4 header without first verifying that the skb contains enough linear data beyond the Ethernet header, matching the root cause.
This is another unsafe IPv4 network-header dereference in the test-run path that could read past truncated skb data.
This directly accesses the IPv6 header without a prior length check, which is unsafe when skb_headlen(skb) only covers the Ethernet header.

The code also gates the access on `switch (skb->protocol)` so the socket family/address setup is conditional on protocol. Because the missing length check is exactly the issue in the root cause, this snippet shows the fix is already present and the vulnerable unchecked dereference is absent.
